notes.summary: Kinematics covers motion in a straight line and in a plane: displacement, velocity, acceleration, the equations of uniformly accelerated motion, motion graphs, vectors, relative velocity, projectile motion and uniform circular motion. NEET tests it through short numericals on the equations of motion, projectile formulas and relative velocity, plus conceptual items on graphs and the vector nature of these quantities.
keyPoints: Equations of uniformly accelerated motion: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as; distance in the nth second sₙ = u + (a/2)(2n − 1). Example: u = 10 m/s to v = 30 m/s over 200 m gives a = 2 m/s².
Slope of x–t graph = velocity; slope of v–t graph = acceleration; area under v–t graph = displacement; area under a–t graph = change in velocity.
Distance ≥ |displacement| and average speed ≥ |average velocity|. Half a revolution on a circle of radius r: distance πr, displacement 2r.
Vector addition: R = √(A² + B² + 2AB cos θ). Forces of 3 N and 4 N at 90° give 5 N; the resultant always lies between |A − B| and A + B.
Projectile (speed u, angle θ): T = 2u sin θ/g, H = u² sin²θ/(2g), R = u² sin 2θ/g. R is maximum (u²/g) at 45°, and angles θ and (90° − θ) give the same range.
Trajectory y = x tan θ − gx²/(2u² cos²θ) is a parabola. At the top, velocity = u cos θ (horizontal) and acceleration = g (vertical), so they are perpendicular.
Relative velocity v(AB) = v(A) − v(B). Rain falling vertically at speed u and a man walking at speed v: tilt the umbrella forward at tan⁻¹(v/u) from the vertical.
River of width d, river speed vr, swimmer speed vs (> vr): minimum time = d/vs (heading straight across, drifts downstream); shortest path (straight across) takes d/√(vs² − vr²).
Uniform circular motion: speed is constant but velocity changes direction; centripetal acceleration a = v²/r = ω²r towards the centre, with v = ωr.
traps: Using cos θ instead of sin θ in time of flight or maximum height — both depend on the vertical component u sin θ.
Saying the velocity is zero at the top of a projectile path; only the vertical component is zero, u cos θ remains.
Forgetting the sign of displacement when a body thrown upward lands below the point of projection (e.g., from a tower).
Confusing minimum-time crossing with shortest-path crossing of a river.
Assuming constant speed means zero acceleration in circular motion.
notes.examTip: Fix a positive direction first and attach a sign to every displacement, velocity and acceleration before substituting into the equations of motion.

questions.text: A particle moves along a circular path of radius 7 m and completes half a revolution. The ratio of the distance travelled to the magnitude of its displacement is:
questions.explanation:
Distance for half a revolution = half the circumference = πr = 7π m.
Displacement = straight line joining the end points = diameter = 2r = 14 m.
Ratio = 7π : 14 = π : 2.

questions.text: A body moves along a circle of radius 2 m with a constant speed of 4 m/s. Its acceleration is:
options: zero, because the speed is constant
questions.explanation:
In uniform circular motion the direction of velocity changes continuously, so there is a centripetal acceleration.
a = v²/r = 4²/2 = 16/2 = 8 m/s².
It is directed towards the centre of the circle.

questions.text: Two forces of magnitudes 3 N and 4 N act on a particle at right angles to each other. The magnitude of their resultant is:
questions.explanation:
R = √(A² + B² + 2AB cos θ) with θ = 90°, and cos 90° = 0.
R = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 N.
7 N would be the resultant only if the forces were parallel, and 1 N only if they were opposite.

questions.text: A car moving with a speed of 10 m/s accelerates uniformly and attains a speed of 30 m/s after covering 200 m. Its acceleration is:
Rain is falling vertically downward with a speed of 4 m/s. A man walks on a horizontal road with a speed of 3 m/s. To protect himself from the rain, he should hold his umbrella:
options: tilted forward, at tan⁻¹(3/4) with the vertical
tilted forward, at tan⁻¹(4/3) with the vertical
tilted backward, at tan⁻¹(3/4) with the vertical
vertically, since the rain falls vertically
questions.explanation:
Velocity of rain relative to the man = velocity of rain − velocity of man.
The relative velocity has a vertical (downward) part of 4 m/s and a horizontal part of 3 m/s opposite to the man's motion, so the rain appears to come from the front.
Angle with the vertical: tan θ = 3/4, so θ = tan⁻¹(3/4) (about 37°).
He should tilt the umbrella forward at tan⁻¹(3/4) with the vertical.

questions.text: A river 100 m wide flows with a speed of 3 m/s. A swimmer can swim at 5 m/s relative to still water. If he wants to cross along the shortest path (to the point directly opposite), the time taken is:
questions.explanation:
For the shortest path, the swimmer heads partly upstream so that his resultant velocity is perpendicular to the bank.
The upstream component must cancel the river: 3 m/s. The across-river component = √(5² − 3²) = √16 = 4 m/s.
Time = width/across speed = 100/4 = 25 s.
(20 s is the minimum time, obtained by heading straight across, but then he drifts downstream.)

questions.text: Two balls are projected from the same point with the same speed, one at 30° and the other at 60° to the horizontal. The ratio of the maximum heights reached (30° ball : 60° ball) is:
questions.explanation:
H = u² sin²θ/(2g); for equal u, H ∝ sin²θ.
sin²30° = 1/4 and sin²60° = 3/4.
H₁ : H₂ = (1/4) : (3/4) = 1 : 3.
(Their ranges are equal because 30° and 60° are complementary angles, which is why 1 : 1 is a trap.)

questions.text: The position vector of a particle moving in a plane is r = 3t î + 2t² ĵ (r in metres, t in seconds). The speed of the particle at t = 1 s is:
questions.explanation:
Velocity v = dr/dt = 3 î + 4t ĵ.
At t = 1 s: v = 3 î + 4 ĵ.
Speed = |v| = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 m/s.
(Adding the components to get 7 m/s ignores that they are perpendicular.)

questions.text:
Assertion (A): A body can have zero velocity at an instant and still have a non-zero acceleration.
Reason (R): Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity and does not depend on the instantaneous value of the velocity.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A ball thrown vertically upward has zero velocity at its highest point, yet its acceleration there is g (9.8 m/s²) downward, so A is true.
Acceleration a = dv/dt depends on how fast the velocity is changing, not on its value at that instant, so R is true.
R directly explains why zero velocity and non-zero acceleration can occur together, so R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.text:
For a projectile launched from level ground at an angle θ (0° < θ < 90°) with the horizontal, consider the following statements (neglect air resistance):
I. At the highest point, the velocity of the projectile is zero.
II. At the highest point, the acceleration of the projectile is g, directed vertically downward.
III. The path of the projectile is a parabola.
IV. At the highest point, the velocity and the acceleration are perpendicular to each other.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
I is false: at the top only the vertical component of velocity is zero; the horizontal component u cos θ remains.
II is true: the only force is gravity, so the acceleration is g downward at every point, including the top.
III is true: y = x tan θ − gx²/(2u² cos²θ) is the equation of a parabola.
IV is true: at the top the velocity is horizontal and g is vertical, so they are at 90°.
Correct statements: II, III and IV only.

questions.text: A stone is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s from the top of a tower 25 m high. Taking g = 10 m/s² and neglecting air resistance, the time after which it hits the ground at the foot of the tower is:
questions.explanation:
Take upward as positive and the top of the tower as origin; the ground is at displacement s = −25 m.
s = ut − ½gt² gives −25 = 20t − 5t².
5t² − 20t − 25 = 0, i.e. t² − 4t − 5 = 0, so (t − 5)(t + 1) = 0.
Rejecting the negative root, t = 5 s.
(4 s is only the time taken to come back to the top of the tower.)
